bounds.domain: One existing supervisor scope, one agent and gateway, one broker and three private publications. Publication failures, cancellation, child exits, readiness timeouts and explicit cleanup failure are included. A retired scope cannot spawn again. Destruction requests and subsequent observations of child termination are distinct.
bounds.assumptions: Readiness is an observed authenticated result. Each startup advance either moves the finite host sequence forward or reports failure/timeout. Cleanup records attempted child destruction and broker closure or explicit failure; it does not acknowledge child exit. Physical termination is an independent environmental observation.
bounds.progress: Startup settles under weak fairness of startup advance, including timeout/failure observation. Retirement returns under weak fairness of cleanup, with explicit failure permitted. Conditional physical-exit progress separately assumes fair observations of each child exit after a destruction request; no unconditional exit acknowledgment is claimed.
bounds.limitations: Does not prove OS scheduling, elapsed deadlines, JVM/Android refinement, file publication durability, secret redaction or a physical-device speedup. One scope abstracts replacement by permanent retirement; concurrent scopes and account-store custody remain outside the model. The existing real-process JVM and loopback tests check implementation boundaries, not every generated trace.

assumptions: Weak fairness of advance, including the host sequence, authenticated readiness observations and bounded-wait failure/timeout observation. No assumption that either child becomes ready.
No fairness. A startup phase may stutter forever.
Weak fairness of cleanup. Settlement includes reported cleanup failure; successful broker closure and process reclamation are not assumed.
No fairness. A retired scope may wait forever for its cleanup outcome.
Weak fairness of advance, including startup failure/deadline or the running supervisor's exit observation. No real observation latency is proved.
No fairness. A stopped child can remain unobserved forever.
No fairness. The modeled scope is never reused after retirement.
Weak fairness of each post-destruction child-termination observation. This assumes eventual observable OS exit and does not establish that destroyForcibly returns only after termination.

No exit-observation fairness. Scope.close can return after requesting destruction; a child exit may remain unobserved forever. Immediate non-quiescence is also covered by the named kill-request scenario.
